A1.justification: Both PDFs describe successive versions of the same geometric forecasting work, renamed from FRIREN to FERN. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices support comparison. Experimental changes and internal inconsistencies do not prevent assessment of the reported revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original forecasting experiments on Lorenz63, Rossler, Lorenz96, ETT, and Weather, together with component and loss-function ablations in Tables 4–13.

after.justification: v4 reports original forecasting results, including Chua’s circuit, component ablations across three datasets, and validation-versus-test checkpoint analysis in Tables 2–11.

M1.justification: v4 introduces 24-step patchwise ellipsoidal transport. Its final transport incorporates fixed complex block factors through U K Lambda K^T U^T, whereas v1 describes a separate Koopman transformation in latent z-space. These are substantive architectural changes beyond renaming, while the ANF-inspired encoding and Huber training objective remain.

E1.justification: Chua’s circuit is added, while the six-dimensional Lorenz96 experiment at forcing F=8 is removed. Lorenz63, Rossler, all four ETT datasets, and Weather remain. This changes the composition of the chaotic benchmarks within the retained forecasting task.

E2.justification: TimeMixer, PatchTST, and DLinear remain the evaluated baselines in corresponding benchmark comparisons. Newly discussed methods such as Koopa and SKOLR are cited for positioning but are not added as experimental comparators.

E3.justification: v4 restricts lookback to 336, reduces Lorenz63/Rossler trajectories from 52,000 to 25,000 steps, changes learning rate/batch size from 9e-4/128 to 3e-4/96, and evaluates ETTh1/2 in original rather than normalized units. It adds grace-period and block-subsampled validation, a composite checkpoint criterion, and horizon-weighted aggregation. Appendix D replaces 500-projection SWD with unprojected component W2; EPT reporting also extends to real-world benchmarks.

E4.justification: v1’s Lorenz63 component and loss studies at horizon 336 are replaced by component tests at horizon 192 across Lorenz63 and ETTh1/2, including new patch, zero-scale, and transport-only controls. v4 adds checkpoint-drift analysis using an earlier FERN variant (Appendix D, Table 11). The Huber/MSE/SWD-weight study, two-encoder exploration, and Lorenz forecast case studies disappear.

E5.justification: v1 reports means and standard deviations over seeds [1955, 7, 20]. v4’s result captions report means and standard errors over [7, 1955, 2023, 4], with aggregated standard errors in Table 1. This revises an existing repeated-run reporting practice. However, v4 Table 13 lists five seeds, leaving the underlying run count inconsistent.

E6.justification: Benchmark and ablation results are extensively replaced, with Chua and checkpoint-analysis results added and Lorenz96 results removed. For example, at Lorenz63 336-in/336-out, v1 Table 4 reports FRIREN MSE 11.4145 and EPT 274.5805; v4 Table 10 reports FERN MSE 21.25 and EPT 187.03. Changed data and experimental settings prevent interpreting these as a same-setting performance deterioration.

T1.justification: v1’s location/shape square-factorization proposition, deterministic MSE–W2 equivalence proposition, and stochastic-MSE decomposition are removed. v4 introduces a Taylor/Jacobian-matching argument and reasoning about SPSD-preserving congruence and restrictions on composing transformations. Takens, Brenier–McCann, and Koopman-invariance background remain, but the substantive mathematical justification changes.

C1.justification: v4 explicitly recasts the work as both a position paper and a model paper, elevating evaluation reform into a core contribution and claiming patchwise ellipsoids represent uncertainty and support regime-shift diagnostics. It also narrows v1’s finite-Koopman-operator claim to a Koopman-inspired construction. The central advocacy of geometric forecasting and chaotic stress tests remains.

C2.justification: v4 adds explanations involving early-validation recency bias, EPT as a measure of dataset predictability, and piecewise-ergodic regimes with ellipsoid width representing uncertainty. It explicitly qualifies the connections to flows, OT, and Koopman theory. v1’s stronger-forcing Lorenz96 and random-walk limitations, and its generative-versus-deterministic interpretation of loss tradeoffs, are removed.

D1.justification: v4 adds pseudocode, detailed network/head specifications, float64-to-float32 simulation instructions, and complexity formulas. It omits v1’s baseline configuration table, chaotic initial conditions, Weather feature-selection details, and direct model-code URL, retaining only a generic code-release reference. Configuration documentation also conflicts: Algorithm 1 and Appendix E specify five encoder stacks, while Table 13 lists six encoder and four decoder stacks.

R1.justification: v4 substantially expands positioning around efficient and frequency-based forecasters, Koopa/SKOLR, stochastic delay embeddings, GradNetOT/ICNN, and invariant-measure learning. It develops explicit distinctions from density modeling, full OT solving, iterated chaos prediction, and system identification, beyond v1’s discussion of ANF, OT, and Koopman foundations.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and method narrative are extensively rewritten, alongside the title and model name. A separate evaluation-protocol section now precedes Methods, references move before the appendices, and the former A.1–A.9 appendix organization becomes separately labeled appendices. Contribution lists and expanded scope discussions substantially reshape the narrative.

P2.justification: v1’s coupling/Koopman diagrams, Lorenz attractor image, and forecast plots are replaced by v4’s three-panel conceptual Figure 1. Result tables are redesigned with simple and horizon-weighted summaries and additional EPT columns. Pseudocode and complexity tables are added, while retained compute measurements move into Table 14. The revised layout also contains several heading-only appendix pages and displaced tables.

improvement.justification: v4 adds useful scope qualifications, cross-dataset component ablations, and checkpoint-selection evidence. However, it loses the loss-tradeoff study and direct code-access instructions, while conflicting architecture and seed descriptions weaken reproducibility. Its Section 4 claim of best ETTm1 MSE also contradicts Table 1, which reports FERN 5.80 versus TimeMixer 5.27. These substantive benefits and reporting deficiencies leave the net direction of overall quality uncertain.
